searchText: Why is it that the single-block reorg attack by delayed block proposal is viable for 30% and ~2% stake https://econcs.pku.edu.cn/wine2020/wine2020/Workshop/GTiB20_paper_8.pdf and here https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.10086# but requires 34% of stake here https://notes.ethereum.org/plgVdz-ORe-fGjK06BZ_3A#Fork-choice-by-block-slot-pair ? Appreciate if anyone could explain? 🙏 In the last paragraph of Vitalik’s post he talks about a 2% balancing attack, so I think it’s just differences in presentation of similar attacks. Pre-proposer boost you didn’t even need 2% to perform a one slot re-org – you could do it with a single vote (per the Three Attacks on PoS Ethereum paper). I think the first paper you linked is also older and less accurate: in point (3) of their strategy they talk about the honest attestations from n+2 competing with the malicious attestations from n+2 but this isn’t necessary because fork choice delays attestations by one slot. So none of the attestations from n+2 influence the head during n+2 which means the contest is between the block from slot n and the delayed re-org block from (n+1) with one extra vote. So the n+1 blocks wins almost every time even with just a single extra vote. All the honest attesters will vote for it in (n+2)
